title: Best Hisense Dehumidifier (2026): 25, 35 & 50-Pint Reviews
dek: Hisense undercuts the big names on price, but skips Wi-Fi entirely and has one model owners complain about. Here's which to buy — and how to fix the E9 code.
description: Hisense dehumidifier reviews for 2026: the best 25, 35 and 50-pint models, which pump model to skip, and fixes for E9 errors and a dirty humidity sensor.
intro: A **Hisense dehumidifier** is often the cheapest way to get a name-brand unit at a given size; the brand's machines are widely stocked and consistently priced below Frigidaire and GE. Our pick for most basements and open rooms is the **Hisense 50-Pint 3-Speed**, which covers up to 4,500 square feet and earns better owner reviews than its pump-equipped sibling.

Two things Hisense's marketing doesn't lead with: **none of its current dehumidifiers offer Wi-Fi or app control**, according to the brand's own product-line page, and its 50-pint pump model draws more owner complaints about sensor errors than the plain version. Below, we rank the current lineup and then tackle the questions owners search for most — the manual, the E9 error code, and how to clean or replace the humidity sensor.
topPicksLead: The **Hisense 50-Pint 3-Speed** is the best Hisense for most homes, covering a full basement without the reliability complaints that dog the pump version.

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compare Hisense's published capacity and coverage claims with DOE and ENERGY STAR data, read the manuals for drainage, defrost and error-code details, check CPSC recall records and look for patterns in owner reviews — in Hisense's case, the cluster of sensor complaints on the pump model shaped our ranking.

We also compare each Hisense with similarly sized units from Frigidaire, Midea and hOmeLabs, since a lower price only matters if the rest of the package holds up. Where Hisense's coverage claims and pint ratings disagree, we size by the square-footage claim and flag the discrepancy.

sections.heading: Hisense dehumidifier repair: E9 code and humidity sensor

blocks.text: Most Hisense repair searches come back to the humidity sensor. Owners commonly report the E9 code as a sensor fault, and a dusty or failing sensor can also make the unit run nonstop or shut off too early. Always check your model's manual for its exact error-code table.
How to clean the humidity sensor on a Hisense dehumidifier

items: Unplug the dehumidifier and remove the water bucket.
Slide out the air filter; the sensor is typically a small component near the air intake, behind the filter or grille.
Remove dust with a soft, dry brush or a few short bursts of compressed air. Don't use water or cleaning sprays.
Wash and fully dry the filter while it's out.
Reassemble, wait a few minutes, and plug the unit back in. Compare the display with a separate hygrometer.

blocks.text: If the E9 code comes back

items: Unplug for 10 minutes to reset the control board, then restart.
Check that the sensor's wire connector hasn't worked loose (only if you're comfortable opening the housing, and only with the unit unplugged).
If the unit is under warranty, contact Hisense support before opening anything — DIY repairs can void coverage.
Out of warranty, a replacement humidity sensor is an inexpensive part; match it to your exact model number from the rating label.

blocks.title: Repair or replace?
blocks.text: A sensor swap is worth doing. A failed compressor or refrigerant leak on an older budget unit usually isn't. Our [how long do dehumidifiers last](/guides/how-long-do-dehumidifiers-last/) guide covers that decision.

The model number is printed on the rating label on the back or side of the unit. Search it on Hisense's U.S. support site to download the user manual, which includes the control-panel guide, error codes and filter instructions. Retailer listings often host the same PDF under "Specifications" or "Documents."
For general troubleshooting that applies to any brand, see our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide.

The **Hisense 50-Pint 3-Speed** is the best Hisense dehumidifier for most basements, without the complaints logged against the pump version. The **25-Pint** is right for a bedroom, the **35-Pint** suits mid-size rooms, and the **50-Pint with Pump** makes sense only when you need the lift. If Wi-Fi is a must, look elsewhere. And if your unit throws an E9 code, start with a gentle sensor cleaning before calling for service.

faqs.q: What is the best Hisense dehumidifier?
faqs.a: The Hisense 50-Pint 3-Speed for most basements and open rooms, covering up to 4,500 square feet. For a bedroom, the 25-Pint ENERGY STAR model.

faqs.q: What does E9 mean on a Hisense dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Owners commonly report E9 as a sensor fault, usually tied to the humidity sensor. Unplug the unit for 10 minutes, clean the sensor area gently, and restart. If it returns, check your manual's error table and contact Hisense support.

faqs.q: How do I clean the humidity sensor on a Hisense dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Unplug it, remove the bucket and filter, and gently clear dust from the sensor near the air intake with a soft dry brush or compressed air. Don't use water. Reassemble and compare the reading with a separate hygrometer.

faqs.q: Is the Hisense 35-pint dehumidifier any good?
faqs.a: It's a reasonable mid-size choice with ENERGY STAR certification, three fan speeds and auto-defrost. Size it by its 3,000 square foot coverage claim rather than the pint figure, which may not reflect the current DOE test.

faqs.q: Where can I find a Hisense dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Find the model number on the unit's rating label and search it on Hisense's U.S. support site. Retailer product pages often host the same PDF.
No current Hisense dehumidifier offers Wi-Fi or app control, according to the brand's product-line page. Midea and hOmeLabs sell connected models.
Usually, if you buy the right model. Owner reviews are good for the non-pump units and they're priced below Frigidaire and GE. The pump model is the one to approach with caution.
